# Fix rules — QA cycle {{cycle}} ({{project}})

<!-- GENERATED by scripts/mkrules.mjs from qa.config.json — edit the config or this template, not the output. Every fixer brief starts with "read and follow FIXRULES.md". -->

You fix ONE named item (or one root-cause group) in your git worktree. Nothing else. Other fixers work in parallel in other worktrees — keep your diff minimal and local; don't refactor shared code you don't need.

## Start
- Create the branch named in your brief from current {{main}} (`git switch -c <id> {{main}}`); note `git rev-parse --short HEAD` as BASE. Handed an existing branch instead: `git merge-base --is-ancestor {{main}} HEAD || git merge --ff-only {{main}}` first. If you're resumed and your branch is already merged, start a fresh branch from {{main}}.
- Read the code around the item before changing it. Reproduce it before fixing it.
- If your brief has a plan, check it isn't stale before coding (see your agent definition); stop with `PLAN GAP — stale` rather than adapting.

## Change rules
- Minimal, focused changes in the surrounding style ({{stack}}).
- One concern per commit, message in the repo's style ({{commitStyle}}), committed with the repo's configured git identity.
  NO Co-Authored-By or any AI trailer. Never push.
- `git stash` is fine (e.g. to manage conflicts), but the stash is shared by every worktree: always `git stash push -u -m <unique-tag>`, restore with `git stash apply <sha>` (find it with `git stash list --format="%H %gs"`), then drop your own entry by tag — never a bare `git stash pop`.
- Add a test that fails before the fix and passes after, wherever the logic is testable without a browser.
- Before finishing: `{{commands.test}}`, `{{commands.lint}}`, `{{commands.build}}` all clean.
{{lines:fixerChange}}

## Running the app
{{lines:fixerRun}}
- Use ONLY your assigned ports ({{ports.fixers}}). Never touch production: {{prod.rule}}
- No real {{thirdParty}} calls. Never read the real secrets file(s): {{join:secrets}}. Stop servers when done (by PID; never pkill by pattern).
- If a command is permission-denied, don't work around it; report it.
- Browser: headless ONLY — never headed, never open a URL on the user's screen.
- Scratch files go under {{scratch}}/fix-<ID>/ (never the bare ID: the verifier's `verify-<ID>/` and APFS's case-insensitivity must not collide; commit real work early).

## Machine load
The machine is shared with the user. Run heavy work serially: one headless browser at a time, never a full test suite while a browser suite runs, and stop every server/browser you start **by PID** as soon as you're done with it.

## Final message
Branch, BASE, `git log --oneline BASE..HEAD`, then one line per item:
`ID FIXED|PARTIAL|NOT FIXED|NOT A BUG|PLAN GAP — what changed — commit — how tested (fails before / passes after, repro before → after)`.
Then residuals as before → after, and anything you couldn't clean up.
